title: The Best Florida Beach Towns for Remote Work (2026)
dek: 31 towns within an hour of an airport where you can walk to coffee, find your people and be on the beach after work.
body:
The best Florida beach towns for remote work are 30A, Delray Beach, Naples and St. Augustine. Each one pairs a walkable center and a real community with a good beach, and each is within about an hour of an airport, without the traffic and prices of a big city.

Everywhere has wifi now, so that is not what makes a remote work town. What matters is whether you can walk to coffee, run into people you know, get to the sand after your last call and still catch a Monday flight. We scored all 167 towns on five things, weighted equally: walkability, restaurants and community, beaches, charm, and how many residents run their own business, from the Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2019 to 2023). Then we kept towns within about an hour of an airport and left out the big cities. 31 towns made it.

1. 30A (Santa Rosa Beach)

30A ranks 2nd of all 167 towns for beaches and 11th for charm, and 7.5% of residents in the Santa Rosa Beach ZIP run their own incorporated business, one of the highest shares on the coast. There is a real scene to plug into, from the Walton Area Chamber's GENERATE business leads group to regular business lunches. Northwest Florida Beaches airport (ECP) is the closest. The catch is price: the typical home is about $915K. See 30A.

2. Delray Beach

Delray is the most complete package on our list: 2nd for walkability, 3rd for restaurants and community and 8th for beaches. Atlantic Avenue runs from downtown straight to the ocean, so breakfast, the beach and a lunch meeting can all happen on one street. Palm Beach airport is the closest. See Delray Beach.

3. Naples

Naples is 4th for beaches and 5th for restaurants and community, with a walkable downtown and Southwest Florida airport (RSW) about 40 minutes away. It is quieter after dark than Delray, and the typical home runs about $685K. See Naples.

4. St. Augustine

St. Augustine is first of all 167 towns for charm and 4th for restaurants and community. It has become a real remote work hub: per AP reporting on Census figures, the share of people working from home in St. Johns County nearly tripled, from 8.6% in 2018 to almost 24% in 2023. Jacksonville (JAX) is about an hour away, and the beach is a bridge over. See St. Augustine.

5. Lauderdale by the Sea

A low rise beach village, 7th for walkability, where 8.1% of residents run their own company. Fort Lauderdale's airport is about 25 minutes away. See Lauderdale by the Sea.

6. Palm Beach

Palm Beach has the highest share of business owners on our list, 10.6% of residents, and Palm Beach airport is about 15 minutes away. It is also the most expensive town we score, with a typical home around $2.7M, and it is quietest in summer. See Palm Beach.

7. Dunedin

Dunedin is 3rd for walkability and 4th for charm, with a downtown right on the Pinellas Trail. Tampa International is within reach, and Caladesi Island's beach is a short ferry ride. The typical home is about $475K. See Dunedin.

8. Vero Beach

Vero is 13th for restaurants and community and 18th for charm, with an oceanside village of shops and a serious arts scene. Melbourne's airport is about 45 minutes away, and homes run about $390K. See Vero Beach.

9. Neptune Beach

Neptune Beach shares Beaches Town Center with Atlantic Beach, with restaurants a block from the sand. It is 15th for restaurants and community, and Jacksonville's airport is about 35 minutes away. See Neptune Beach.

10. Fernandina Beach

Fernandina is 3rd for charm and 6th for walkability, with a Victorian downtown on Centre Street and uncrowded beaches near the Georgia line. JAX is about 40 minutes away. See Fernandina Beach.

The rest of the list

Venice, New Smyrna Beach, Anna Maria Island, Key West, St. Pete Beach, Sanibel, Stuart, Clearwater Beach, Treasure Island, St. Augustine Beach, Atlantic Beach, Tarpon Springs, Boca Raton, Lake Worth Beach, Jacksonville Beach, Fort Myers Beach, Siesta Key, Wilton Manors, Bradenton Beach, Gulfport and Sarasota round out the 31. Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach are still rebuilding from Hurricane Ian, so visit before you buy. Island and beach strip towns like Anna Maria, Siesta Key and Treasure Island lean on a bigger downtown nearby for coworking and errands.

How we picked them

Each town gets a rank from 1 to 167 on walkability, restaurants and community, beaches and charm from our own town scores, plus a rank for the share of residents who run their own incorporated business (US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019 to 2023, table B24080). We averaged the five, kept towns within about an hour of an airport, and left out the big cities. Towns with fewer than 500 workers do not have a reliable business number, so they are scored on the other four. See every town on the Vibe Map, or read our guide to the most walkable beach towns.
faq: What is the best Florida beach town for remote work?
30A tops our 2026 list, with top ranked beaches, real charm, a strong business community and Northwest Florida Beaches airport nearby. Delray Beach, Naples and St. Augustine are close behind.
Which remote work town is closest to an airport?
Palm Beach, about 15 minutes from Palm Beach airport, then Lauderdale by the Sea, about 25 minutes from Fort Lauderdale's airport.
What is the most affordable Florida beach town for remote work?
Of the 31 on our list, Venice (about $384K), Vero Beach (about $390K) and Gulfport (about $400K) have the lowest typical home prices.
Is St. Augustine good for remote workers?
Yes. Per AP reporting on Census figures, the share of St. Johns County workers who work from home nearly tripled to almost 24% between 2018 and 2023.
